title: The problem is with a wearable backpack in Unreal Engine.
author: BeyondFar3584
selftext:
Hi everyone!  
I’m writing because I’ve been struggling with an issue that I haven’t been able to solve, despite spending several full days working on it with Astra.  
I have a rigged 3D character that can run, jump, and crouch, but I can’t seem to get a backpack to work properly on the character.  
Whenever I try, the shoulder straps twist and deform in weird ways, they don’t interact or collide properly with the character’s clothing, and the animations for putting the backpack on and taking it off look absolutely terrible.  
Has anyone dealt with something similar or found a reliable way to make this work?

comments.author: ProbablyDoesntLikeU
comments.body: Well first off id try opus over astra

replies.author: ProbablyDoesntLikeU
replies.body: Also random, but I'd suggest having the backpack straps be static, or at least bounded. A fully physics enabled backpack is excessive

replies.author: BeyondFar3584
replies.body: I kept the whole backpack rigid but I can't integrate the shoulder straps and make them move with the character, they deform, make strange turns and they don't seem to support the weight of the backpack. 😭

replies.author: jshmoe866
replies.body: Keep the straps fixed tk the character model and if you’re ambitious have the clothes under them ruffle slightly. That might get the effect you’re going for without having to give the backpack it’s own physics

replies.author: ProbablyDoesntLikeU
replies.body:
https://github.com/ADD-Attack/moorefolio/blob/backpack-straps-demo/TECHNIQUE.md

Try this. But yeah, you are better off eliminatimg expensive features that serve no purpose rather than over engineering solutions to problems that don't exist. But more power to you

comments.author: duskaception
comments.body: Honestly bro I just said fuck shoulder strap. Just slap it to the back. Same for weapons just slap those to the side of the backpack floating there (not floating but no obvious straps)
